TSN and Sportsnet land long-term NBA rights renewals in Canada
article_text:
TSN and Sportsnet, the Canadian pay-TV broadcasters, have renewed their long-standing rights deals with basketball’s NBA through 2035-36.

Under the 10-year deals, Bell Media’s sports-focused TSN and Rogers-owned Sportsnet will continue to share the 82 regular-season games involving the Toronto Raptors, Canada’s only NBA franchise, with each airing 41 games.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

TSN also retained “extensive coverage of matchups from around the league”, while Sportsnet announced it will continue to air marquee events, including the NBA Playoffs and NBA Finals, as well as “hundreds of other matchups airing nationally.”

The deals come amid the NBA’s 11-year global rights deal with Prime Video, the streaming platform of e-commerce giant Amazon, which began with the 2025-26 season.

The deal sees it air 66 regular-season games, the NBA Cup, the Play-In tournament, select first-and second-round playoff games, and Conference Finals in Canada.

As part of its package, for the first time in Raptors history, select regular-season games have been made exclusive to Prime Video rather than airing on traditional Canadian carriers.

Prime Video is also offering NBA League Pass, the NBA’s subscription service for streaming live and on-demand games.

The new long-term deal consolidates TSN’s basketball portfolio for the next decade, having secured rights in the country to FIBA competitions, Canada Basketball games, as well as the matchups involving the WNBA’s Toronto Tempo.

title: DAZN secures ‘option on’ 2029 FIFA Club World Cup streaming rights
article_text:
DAZN has secured an exclusive option on the global streaming rights to the 2029 FIFA Club World Cup, according to the Guardian. The deal extends the streaming platform’s relationship with football’s world governing body.

DAZN paid $1bn (£745m) for the global rights to the first 32-team Club World Cup, held in the US in 2025. Its bid came late, after several linear broadcasters and streaming services had declined to bid. Apple TV had held talks with FIFA but withdrew over valuation, and FIFA’s attempt to sell the rights region by region did not succeed.

That deal was supported by Saudi Arabia’s Surj Sports Investment, which bought a 10% stake in DAZN, and in effect funded the tournament’s $1bn prize pot. Champions Chelsea received around $114m (£85m).

DAZN has more than 300m registered users but remains loss-making. Its 2025 accounts show operating losses rising from $772.9m to $939.8m year on year.

Planning for the 2029 edition remains at an early stage. FIFA has not confirmed the venue, format or size of the tournament, although expanding it to 48 teams has been under discussion with clubs.

Progress has been held back by tensions between FIFA and European Football Clubs (EFC), the body representing Europe’s leading clubs. According to the Guardian, EFC has raised concerns with FIFA over delays in paying $250m in solidarity money owed to clubs from the 2025 tournament. The two sides have yet to agree terms for a proposed joint venture to run the competition’s commercial operations, and that work may wait until after the FIFA presidential election in March.

Morocco, a co-host of the 2030 World Cup, is seen as the leading candidate to stage the 2029 tournament. Its case has been strengthened by FIFA’s decision to award the first women’s Club World Cup to the US, which had also been in contention for 2029. A joint bid from Morocco and Spain is also possible.

The value of the option, and the date by which DAZN must take it up, have not been disclosed.

title: England team to face Australia: Henry Pollock left out as Borthwick makes big calls
article_text:
England will kick off their Nations Championship campaign against Australia at Allianz Stadium this weekend.

Steve Borthwick's side won two of their three matches in the competition and will be eager to put themselves in the strongest possible position ahead of the finals weekend, which will also take place at Allianz Stadium.

Following the squad announcement yesterday evening, we take a look at how England could line up for their opening encounter with the Wallabies.

The front row looks relatively straightforward, with Ellis Genge and Joe Heyes expected to continue as the starting props. Both have impressed enough to retain their places and remain among the first names on the teamsheet.

Jamie George gets the nod at hooker ahead of Luke Cowan-Dickie, having enjoyed the better run of form recently. However, this is an area Borthwick may need to address in the coming months, with both experienced internationals now entering the latter stages of their careers.

Maro Itoje returns to the second row after a well-earned rest. He has looked refreshed in his early-season performances for Saracens and should also reclaim the captaincy.

He is joined by new Saracens teammate George Martin, who brings enormous physicality and impressed when given his opportunities over the summer. His performance against South Africa was particularly encouraging, showing he can compete with the very best.

In the back row, Ollie Chessum starts at blindside flanker, which increasingly looks like his best position.

Leaving Henry Pollock out will divide opinion, but Tom Curry's experience could prove crucial against Australia.

Pollock has made a huge impact in an England shirt, although Borthwick may prefer to unleash him against tiring defenders.

Ben Earl completes the back row at No.8. His carrying ability and mobility offer an excellent balance alongside Chessum and Curry. Starting Pollock instead of Curry could leave the pack looking slightly lightweight.

Provided he is fully fit, Fin Smith should be the clear choice at fly-half.

He is partnered by Jack van Poortvliet, who appears to have moved ahead of Ben Spencer in the pecking order.

In midfield, we predict Borthwick will turn to a strong club partnership in Seb Atkinson and Will Joseph.

The pair have shown they complement each other extremely well and could provide the answer to England's ongoing centre problem.

With plenty of chopping and changing in recent months, having two players who regularly play alongside each other at club level would offer some much-needed consistency.

The selection of Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tommy Freeman on the wings should come as little surprise, with both expected to retain their places.

Finally, George Furbank gets the nod at full-back ahead of Marcus Smith. Now teammates at Harlequins, Furbank offers a more natural option in the position.

Rather than continuing to shoehorn players into unfamiliar roles, selecting Furbank at 15 makes sense, while Smith could provide a significant attacking threat off the bench.

'Fully loaded' All Blacks out to preserve Scotland record
article_text:
New Zealand assistant Mike Blair says the All Blacks will come to Murrayfield "fully loaded" as they seek to preserve their unbeaten record against Scotland on Saturday.

With recent meetings between the sides decided by single-digit margins, Blair says there is a respect for the threat the Scots will pose in the Nations Championship meeting.

"When I played, New Zealand played their second-string team. They gave guys opportunity against us," he said.

"Times have changed from that. We're fully loaded. We're ready to go."

In 33 attempts and 121 years of trying, Scotland have never beaten the All Blacks, and as desperate as they are to end that barren run, New Zealand are just as keen to protect their unblemished record.

"It's really important," said Blair, who played 85 times for Scotland and was head coach of Edinburgh from 2021 to 2023.

"We've got a couple of long-standing records. The Eden Park record [the All Blacks have not lost a Test there since 1994], every time we play there, there's an extra edge to it because you don't want to be the team that loses that record. It's definitely a huge motivation.

"We're really proud of that record [against Scotland]. We know over the last four matches it's been close, so it's going to be a tough contest for sure."

Having worked under Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend with both Glasgow Warriors and Scotland, Blair retains a strong relationship with his former international team-mate.

"We've been in touch this week," Blair said. "When I was over after the fourth Test [against South Africa], I was over for a couple of weeks and caught up with them and make a point to do that.

"We're just a little bit more cagey around certain things, how we believe the game's developing now and what we can do, because obviously we're up against each other now and I think we play each other before the World Cup as well.

"You need to be aware of certain plays the opposition might do over shape, but you've really got to trust what you're trying to do. I certainly feel like that with attack, you'll make little tweaks in your detail depending on what the defence offer, but if we get our game right then we can impose ourselves.

"So there's a bit of inside knowledge but I don't think it carries a huge amount of weight."

Blair says the squad and staff are still coming to terms with the shock death of the All Blacks head of security, Logan Cadwallader.

Cadwallader passed away suddenly on Sunday following the squad's arrival in Edinburgh, with head coach Rennie saying "we are all devastated".

"It's been a tough couple of days," said Blair.

"Logan was a big part of the All Blacks for 10 years and very close with players and management and obviously a huge, huge shock and it's taken time to deal with."

title: Westwood 'unemployed' amid LIV uncertainty as Rahm discusses exit
article_text:
Lee Westwood says he has not signed for LIV 2.0 or held talks with the DP World Tour about a return, leaving the European Ryder Cup legend "unemployed" as he considers his future.

The 53-year-old Englishman was among the high-profile players lured to LIV Golf when the controversial Saudi-backed breakaway tour began in 2022.

LIV's future remains unclear after Saudi's Public Investment Fund (PIF) withdrew its backing - having pumped in more than $5bn (£3.8bn) - and led to the league filing for bankruptcy protection last month.

It has secured a possible $300m (£224m) in financing from BC Partners Credit to try to move forward with LIV 2.0, but only a handful of players have so far committed to the proposed competition in 2027.

In an interview with The Chipping Forecast podcast,, external Westwood said: "I'm currently unemployed.

"There hasn't been anything presented to me that is agreeable for LIV 2.0, there are still a lot of things on that which need fine-tuning. I haven't signed for 2.0. I haven't signed anything."

Westwood has been heavily criticised for pursuing the vast sums of money offered by LIV.

The move cost him the chance to captain the European Ryder Cup in 2023, but he says he would have "been stupid" not to set himself up financially for life.

"I've made a fortune over the last four and a half years," added Westwood, who is reported to have won £16m in prize money on the LIV tour.

"I don't really have to play golf again, but I still love playing golf so it's given the option what to do over the next few years."

Rahm unwilling to 'follow path' of LIV 2.0

Fellow European Ryder Cup player Jon Rahm says he decided to leave LIV because he "wasn't willing to follow the path" taken by the league as it fights for survival.

It was the first time the 31-year-old Spaniard has spoken publicly since securing his exit from the series in October by reaching a separation agreement.

Rahm was the reigning Masters champion when he was convinced to join LIV - a seismic move which underlined the scale of the league's ambition.

"As much as I liked the project and the idea on, let's say, LIV 1.0, I wasn't thrilled with the changes they were doing to 2.0," Rahm said at the Abu Dhabi Championship, his first event since leaving LIV.

"It wasn't anything special, anything that stood out. I just didn't like where they were going with 2.0."

Rahm joined LIV in a deal worth a reported $300m (£222m), only to leave last month with $100m (£75m) - according to ESPN - owed on the remainder of the contract.

"There were too many unknowns," added the two-time major winner. "It seemed like it was going a bit away from team golf.

"It became more of a regular tournament. It wasn't really ever much of a consideration."

Rahm is among several big-name players to leave LIV in recent weeks, along with Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton and Graeme McDowell.

Westwood remains unsure what he will do next, but he does believe the proposed LIV 2.0 still has the potential to thrive.

"With the way the business was structured, there was too much waste really," he said.

"I think there is a business there - if LIV 2.0 gets off the ground it will be a successful business. Can they get the players? Time will tell."

If Westwood does not rejoin LIV, the former world number one could look for a way back to the DP World Tour.

Westwood is a giant of European golf, having won 25 times on the tour and played in 11 Ryder Cups, but an attempt to rejoin the fold would require patience.

Westwood could only return if he accepts a 10-tournament suspension, which was imposed as punishment for resigning his membership when he joined LIV.

"I'm yet to have everything put out in front of me. I've not really had any sort of dialogue with the European Tour," Westwood added.

"I know that if I sign up on 12 November, I've got to serve a 10-tournament suspension, which takes me through the South African Open.

"The first event I could play would be Turkey in May. But I'm not even sure about that yet."

title: 'Wasn't thrilled with the changes': Jon Rahm explains why he 'rejected' LIV 2.0
article_text:
Weeks have gone by since we learned Jon Rahm was leaving LIV Golf after three years with the upstart league. We only knew that based on statements his lawyers made in LIV bankruptcy court. We hadn’t heard anything directly from Rahm.

But that changed in a big way on Tuesday.

Rahm is making the first start of his post-LIV career at the DP World Tour’s Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship this week, and on Tuesday he sat down for his first press conference as a former LIV Golf pro.

In responses to reporters’ questions, Rahm revealed both the specific reasons he wasn’t interested in signing up for LIV 2.0 and discussed the possibility of making a PGA Tour return in 2027.

On Tuesday morning in Abu Dhabi, Rahm opened his first response by calling his three years with LIV Golf, which he joined in 2023 on a reported nine-figure deal, “a wonderful experience,” saying he “played a lot of good golf” during his time with the league.

Then, when pressed for details on why he decided to leave LIV, Rahm revealed that while he loved the original LIV, he was not “thrilled” with the plans for LIV 2.0.

“Why I rejected the terms? As much as I liked the project and the idea on, let’s say, LIV 1.0, I wasn’t thrilled with the changes they were doing to 2.0 and I just wasn’t willing to follow that path, right. It wasn’t anything special, anything that stood out,” Rahm explained.

He continued: “I just, yeah, I didn’t like what they were going with 2.0.”

As far as we know, the current vision for LIV 2.0 involves a shorter season with fewer events and smaller prize purses. A 10-event schedule has been floated, five of which would be team events.

But at this point, those are simply visions. Nothing has been formally decided. LIV is still trying to land commitments from players to secure full investments for the future. As commitment deadlines have come and gone, star players continue to flee LIV, mostly to rejoin the DP World Tour full-time.

The lack of certainty around LIV’s future played a big role in Rahm’s decision to depart, as did changes that Rahm claimed make LIV more of a “regular tour.”

“Too many unknowns at the time and there are still quite a few. It seemed like it was going away from team golf and some of the things that made LIV, LIV. It just became more of a regular tour,” Rahm said on Tuesday.

For those reasons, Rahm revealed that he never seriously considered signing up for LIV 2.0.

“So yeah, it wasn’t really ever much of a consideration to be honest,” he said.

Now the question for Rahm is this: what’s next?

The DP World Tour is Rahm’s most obvious avenue for playing time, and he confirmed as much on Tuesday, saying the tour has been “really gracious” in allowing him to play its events, like this week’s Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, the season’s first playoff event.

As for the PGA Tour, Rahm admitted “things are a little bit different.”

He said he has not yet started negotiations with the PGA Tour over a possible 2027 return, and until he does, his plan is to play the full season in Europe.

“So I have yet to have a discussion with the PGA Tour to see if there’s any path back for next year,” Rahm explained. “So I don’t know, as of right now. Until I get clarity on that, yeah, my plan would be to spend the year on the DP World Tour, and I’m looking forward to it.”

Rahm is not the first LIV star to leave with the hopes of making a PGA Tour return. One year ago, Brooks Koepka ended his LIV career and rejoined the PGA Tour via the Returning Member Program. That avenue was open to Rahm as well last year, but he declined it. That route is closed now, and Rahm acknowledged he’s facing “different circumstances” than Koepka did.

“I don’t know what is in store for us. We know what they did with Brooks [Koepka]. This is different circumstances. I don’t know what things are going to look like,” Rahm said on Tuesday.

Later in his press conference, Rahm openly pondered whether Koepka’s path back to the PGA Tour could open back up for him.

“I haven’t really gone too deeply into it just because there’s still a question mark, right. Obviously Brooks was able to go back through certain circumstances. I don’t know if the possibility of that would be open for me or not,” Rahm said. “But if I have to fulfill a one-year suspension, I think it’s a pretty good position to be that a worst-case scenario I get to play on a wonderful tour for a whole year.”

Even if he is granted an accelerated pathway back to the PGA Tour, where he’s won 11 times, Rahm declared that he would still play DP World Tour events to support the European circuit.

“I will be supporting the tour, for sure, and even if I get to go and play PGA Tour events, I’ll still play European Tour events, as well,” Rahm said. “I’ll play some events that I want to play like I’ve done in the past and maybe a few more.”

While LIV 2.0 is in dire straits, the Rahm 2.0 era officially begins on Thursday.

title: Jon Rahm uncertain about PGA Tour future after LIV Golf exit but would accept deal similar to Brooks Koepka to return
article_text:
Jon Rahm is aware his route back to the PGA Tour is a complicated one and while doubtful he would be once again offered the same deal as Brooks Koepka, he said he would "probably take the penalties".

Rahm quit LIV Golf after deeming the terms offered for the proposed relaunch of the breakaway series "unacceptable".

This occurred when LIV Golf was going through Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the US after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support at the end of the season, having invested $5bn (£3.7bn) over four years.

Having now left LIV, Rahm is set to return to play on the DP World Tour in 2027, but expressed some uncertainty over his future, admitting he has not yet spoken to the PGA Tour about what a return could look like.

At the beginning of 2026, Rahm declined the PGA Tour's offer of reinstatement through a specially created Returning Member Program, which was made available to him, Bryson DeChambeau, Cameron Smith and Brooks Koepka.

Koepka was the only player to sign up to the Returning Member Program.

"As of right now, I really don't know what 2027 is going to look like for me," Rahm said, speaking ahead of the DP World Tour's Abu Dhabi Championship, live on Sky Sports from Thursday.

"I have yet to have a discussion with the PGA Tour to see if there's any path back for next year, so I don't know.

"Until I get clarity on that, my plan would be to spend a year on the DP World Tour. I'm looking forward to it.

"Obviously, Brooks [Koepka] was able to go back through certain circumstances.

"I don't know if the possibility of that would be open for me or not."

As part of the Returning Member Program, Koepka returned to the PGA Tour under certain conditions, with the American instructed to make a $5m (£3.7m) charitable donation and was excluded from earning equity on the PGA Tour for the next five years.

At present, Rahm will face a one-year suspension from the PGA Tour before he is eligible to win back his card.

"If I have to fulfil a one-year suspension, it's a pretty good position to be in. Worst-case scenario, I get to play in a wonderful tour [the DP World Tour] for a whole year," Rahm added.

"I seriously doubt I will get offered the same deals that Brooks did. But if I got offered exactly the same penalties as him, I probably would do it, yes."

Rahm, who tees up at this week's Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, reflected on his time with LIV Golf positively, but he admitted he did not like the direction the new iteration of the league was heading in, and in the end, it was not much of a "consideration" on whether to stay.

For Rahm, a move away from the team golf element was a big factor.

"Well, I would say I can only reflect on those three years as a positive. It was a wonderful experience; I played a lot of good golf, obviously, individually and as a team. We did great," he added.

"Why did I reject the terms? As much as I liked the project and the idea on, let's say, LIV 1.0, I wasn't thrilled with the changes they were doing to 2.0, and I just wasn't willing to follow that path.

"It wasn't anything special, anything that stood out. I didn't like what they were going with 2.0.

"There were too many unknowns at the time, and there's still quite a few.

"It seemed like it was going a bit away from team golf and some of the things that made LIV. It just became more of a regular tour.

"It wasn't really ever much of a consideration, to be honest."

title: TNT Sports and 5 Secure UK Broadcast Rights for Cricket Australia 2026/2027 Down Under Season
article_text:
Pay-television broadcaster TNT Sports and free-to-air network 5 have secured a sub-licensing and broadcast rights agreement with Cricket Australia to deliver exclusive live and free-to-air coverage of the upcoming 2026/2027 Australian domestic international season to viewers across the United Kingdom.

Under the agreement, TNT Sports holds exclusive live broadcast rights for England’s white-ball tour of Australia during the 2026/2027 winter season, alongside high-profile international series featuring New Zealand.

Free-to-air broadcaster 5 will provide dedicated free-to-air highlights packages across its linear channel and digital streaming platforms following every fixture of England’s limited-overs campaign.

The Cricket Australia deal significantly expands TNT Sports’ international cricket portfolio, complementing existing long-term rights agreements to broadcast New Zealand’s home internationals and India’s home international fixtures, including Australia’s five-Test tour of India scheduled for early 2027.

In the UK, TNT Sports will distribute live coverage via its streaming service on HBO Max (available via a standalone 12-month plan for £25.99 per month) alongside linear television distribution across EE TV, Prime Video, Sky, and Virgin Media platforms.

title: England call up Spencer and Randall as injuries hit Wallabies prep
article_text:
Ben Spencer and Harry Randall have been named in England's squad for this month's Nations Championship after injury ruled Northampton nines Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland out of Sunday's match with Australia.

Mitchell pulled up with a hamstring issue in Saints' win over Gloucester on Saturday, while uncapped prospect McParland, 21, picked up a calf injury in last week's training camp.

McParland, who would have toured with England in July but for a severe cut to his leg in the Prem final win over Exeter, could still be in contention for England's matches against Japan and New Zealand on 14 and 21 November respectively.

Mitchell will have a scan on his hamstring on Monday to assess the extent of his injury and subsequent lay-off.

The 29-year-old has suffered three previous hamstring injuries already this year.

Leicester's Jack van Poortvliet, who started all three of England's summer Tests, seems set to continue as first-choice scrum-half.

England are facing a possible change at fly-half, with first-choice Fin Smith struggling with a calf problem and Marcus Smith and George Ford competing to deputise in his possible absence.

Elsewhere Saracens' Theo Dan has seen off competition from Nathan Jibulu, Jamie Blamire and Gabriel Oghre to secure the third hooker spot in the squad.

Dan comes in in place of Bath's Kepu Tuipulotu who, like McParland, picked up an injury during last week's three-day training camp.

Gloucester centre Seb Atkinson and Exeter wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso are also included after successfully negotiating injury comebacks for their clubs this weekend.

Midfield is the area of most selection intrigue with Gloucester's Will Joseph, who won his solitary previous cap back in 2022, and Sale's Joe Marchant, who has returned to eligibility after three seasons playing in France, included.

Bath centre pair Ollie Lawrence and Max Ojomoh, who both starred in last autumn's clean sweep, are omitted and there is no space for 20-year-old Saracens wing Noah Caluori.

After the matches against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, England will play a fourth Test against an as-yet-undecided southern hemisphere opponent in the play-off finals weekend of the new Nations Championship format.

title: Rassie Erasmus unveils established Springboks side for Italy battle in Turin
article_text:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has named a familiar-looking side to take on Italy at Allianz Stadium in Turin on Saturday, featuring several experienced players in the starting lineup.

The Springboks head to Turin following their recent defeat to the Wallabies in Perth, which ended a three-Test winning streak, after beating the All Blacks 3-1 in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

Erasmus’ men currently sit top of the Southern Hemisphere table in the Nations Championship, with three wins from three Tests in July. The Springboks comfortably beat England 45-21, before claiming a 42-28 win over Scotland and a 43-point win over Wales.

Inspirational captain Siya Kolisi will lead the Springboks, alongside Pieter-Steph du Toit and Jasper Wiese in the back row.

It’s an experienced front row, with Malcolm Marx, Ox Nche, and Thomas Du Toit named to start, with Salmaan Moerat and Ruan Nortje in the second row.

Morne van den Berg and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu will line up in the 9-10 combination, while Erasmus has gone with the formidable combination of Jesse Kriel and Damian De Allende in the midfield.

Ethan Hooker and Kurt-Lee Arendse get the nod on the wings, with Damian Willemse returning from a recent injury to start at fullback.

The Springboks head coach said they are not underestimating Italy, who have “quality forwards and backline players”.

“Italy are a quality team who will enter this match with immense motivation with an eye on trying to start their home leg on a positive note in front of their home crowd, and they have challenged us well before, so we have no doubt they will come out passionate and driven as ever,” said Erasmus.

“They have quality forwards and backline players, and although they are missing a few key players due to injury, they have a talented squad with players who will certainly want to make their mark with the 2027 Rugby World Cup less than a year away, so they will give everything on Saturday.

“The vital factors for us, however, will be to be accurate in our execution and to play for the full 80 minutes, especially given the high stakes at the end of these three pool matches.

“Make no mistake though, they will be raring to go, not only with the Nations Cup in mind, but also to take full advantage of these matches as all the participating teams in the competition are preparing for the Rugby World Cup next year.”

The 53-year-old head coach said they have gone for a “battle-hardened” group, to continue the momentum from the July Nations Championship window, and Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry.

“We have three challenging matches ahead if we want to advance to the last game of the Finals Weekend, so our next three matches are going to be vital to lay a strong foundation for the tour.

“All our energy is focused on the match against Italy for now. Fortunately, some of the Japan-based players were able to travel to Italy earlier than the rest of the squad, so they have been working with some of the coaching staff for a few days already and are fully in the swing of things, while we had our first training session on Monday afternoon, so everyone is now on the same page.

“With the majority of the squad having played together for most of the season, we are confident that the players who participated in the Vodacom United Rugby Championship and French Top 14 will ease into things seamlessly this week at training.

“The fact that they are battle-hardened after a few tough matches will offer us a good balance with fresh players raring to go and others who come off a few challenging matches for their franchises and clubs.”

title: EBU and World Aquatics in six-year extension
article_text:
The European Broadcasting Union (EBU) umbrella body of free-to-air broadcasters on the continent has extended its tie-up with the World Aquatics governing body.

Through a six-year contract renewal between the two parties – unveiled today – 23 EBU members will have access to a range of top-tier World Aquatics events and tournaments through until 2032. The agreement stretches across linear TV, digital platforms, and social media.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The tie-up covers – at the time of writing – EBU members in the following countries: Albania, Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Lithuania, North Macedonia, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Serbia, Slovakia, Switzerland, and Turkiye.

The previous deal between the EBU and World Aquatics was unveiled in mid-2024 as only a two-year affair. Both have been brokered by the Sportfive agency (which holds international media distribution rights for World Aquatics).

This new tie-up covers events including the World Aquatics Championships in 2027, 2029, and 2031, as well as the World Aquatics Swimming Championships in 2028, 2030, and 2032.

The 2027 Championships are set to take place in Budapest, Hungary, between June 26 and July 18.

Glen Killane, EBU Sport's executive director, commented: "With Los Angeles 2028 on the horizon, and Brisbane 2032 to follow, our members will bring audiences across Europe closer to the world's leading aquatic athletes as they build towards the next Olympic Games, sharing the performances and stories that shape their journeys.

Brent Nowicki, executive director at World Aquatics, added: “Aquatic sports continue to generate widespread engagement, and with a number of milestone events on the horizon, increased coverage across television and digital platforms will be instrumental in raising the profile of our sports and showcasing our world-class athletes.

“We’re excited to see how the continuation of our partnership will enable us to drive further growth in the years to come, through pinnacle events such as the World Aquatics Championships Budapest 2027."

In terms of recent EBU sports rights activity, mid-October saw the umbrella body announce a two-year extension of its tie-up with Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO), the rights-holder for some of the biggest road cycling events on the continent.

In September, the body also extended its rights tie-up with the International Biathlon Union (IBU) until 2034.

The World Aquatics-Sportfive deal, meanwhile, dates back to mid-2023.

title: Topgolf partners with Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy’s TMRW Sports
article_text:
Topgolf has signed a multi-year partnership with TMRW Sports, bringing experiences from its TGL and WTGL team golf leagues to Topgolf venues and Toptracer Range facilities worldwide.

Under the agreement, fans at Topgolf venues will be able to play the custom-designed competition holes used in TGL and WTGL matches for the first time. Selected venues will host watch parties on match nights, and promotions will offer prizes including greenside tickets, VIP Clubhouse access and suite nights at SoFi Center, the leagues’ home in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida.

The partnership launches alongside WTGL’s first season, which begins on 8th November. The Topgolf WTGL Challenge lets guests play holes from WTGL matches throughout the season, with three randomly drawn players each winning a $500 voucher for WTGL merchandise. The prize draw runs from 8th November to 23rd December.

The deal also covers Topgolf Media Networks, Topgolf’s recently launched sponsorship, media and licensing division. TGL and WTGL will feature in a campaign across email, social media and more than 28,000 digital screens at Topgolf’s US venues. Toptracer already provides the ball-tracking technology for TGL and WTGL broadcasts.

TMRW Sports was co-founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy. Created with the PGA Tour, TGL features teams of PGA Tour players. WTGL, run with the LPGA, will have five teams in its first season. Topgolf says the partnership supports its target of creating 10m new committed golfers by 2030.

David McKillips, CEO of Topgolf and Toptracer, said, “TGL and WTGL are redefining how modern fans consume golf, which aligns perfectly with our mission to make the game more accessible through tech-driven innovation. Through our partnership with TMRW Sports, our Topgolf venues and Toptracer Range partners are able to turn casual viewers into active participants by giving millions of players a taste of TGL and WTGL action in real time.”

Rufus Hack, President, Golf at TMRW Sports, said, “Fans won’t just watch our leagues, they’ll get to play them. Together, we can give fans more ways to experience TGL and WTGL, take on the same holes as the pros and stay connected well beyond match night.”

Former England Sevens coach Simon Amor returns to RFU
article_text:
Simon Amor will return to the Rugby Football Union as interim head of women’s performance at the start of 2027.

He will stand in for Charlie Hayter, who will have taken up the role as general manager of high performance with the British & Irish Lions ahead of the 2027 Howden Lions Women’s Tour of New Zealand.

Hayter, a former England Sevens international, will continue in a hybrid role until March before Amor assumed full oversight of the Red Roses and pathway programmes. He will oversee their Six Nations campaign and preparations for WXV Global Series 2027.

“It’s great to be back with the RFU at such an exciting time for women’s rugby and to work with Mitch again,” Amor said.

“Having worked with some of the players during my time with England Sevens, I know what a special group this is and am excited to support their ambition to reach even higher performance levels. I’m also looking forward to supporting the pathway and the next generation of English talent, while contributing to the continued growth of the PWR.

“I’m delighted for both Charlie and Jo [Yapp, Lions Women head coach], who I’ve worked with previously, and I’m relishing the opportunity to play my part in driving the women’s game forward.”

Amor’s career has seen him work across men’s and women’s rugby. An England Sevens captain in his own playing career, he went on to coach London Scottish and was named head coach of England Women’s Sevens in 2007.

In 2013, Amor was named head coach of England Men’s Sevens and led Great Britain’s men to a silver medal at the 2016 Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro. In his role as Head of England Sevens, Amor oversaw both programmes and secured qualification for the 2020 Games in Tokyo.

Later appointed Eddie Jones’ attack coach in 2020 – during which time he helped England men to a 2020 Guinness Six Nations title – Amor has since worked with Hong Kong China, Japan and the USA.

Conor O’Shea, RFU Director of Performance, added: “We are delighted that Simon has agreed to come into this role whilst Charlie and Jo are away with the inaugural B&I Lions.

“Simon brings with him huge credibility and knowledge and we know that he will come into this role to challenge and make a difference which is massively important to us as we evolve both the Red Roses, and our pathway, on the road to 2029 in Australia. We are all excited to welcome Simon back in the New Year.”

title: Fery suffers first-round defeat in Paris Masters
article_text:
Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery suffered defeat by Quentin Halys in the first round of the Paris Masters.

Halys, 30, competing in the final ATP Masters 1000 event of the season, produced an impressive display to beat the Briton 7-6 (8-6) 7-5.

Both players held serve throughout the opening set, with Halys eventually winning the tie-break after saving two set points.

The Frenchman, who impressed on serve in particular, then fended off two break points early in the second set.

An excellent lob from Fery saved Halys' first break point in an eight-minute service game midway through the set.

Halys then showed his class by saving another break point to hold serve as Fery pushed to force a deciding set.

A superb forehand winner finally earned Halys a break, allowing him to serve for the match.

He sealed victory with a fitting ace and will now face seventh seed Frances Tiafoe, who received a first-round bye.

Alongside a memorable Wimbledon run, Fery missed out on his first ATP 250 tournament title after losing the Winston-Salem Open final to Ignacio Buse in August.

title: McDonald’s Says Goodbye to FIFA After 32 Years: What Failed in Its Largest World Cup Campaign? - Portada-online.com
article_text:
This article has been provided by Portada’s sister publication Adtech.com

One of sports marketing’s most iconic partnerships is coming to an end. McDonald’s has chosen not to renew its World Cup sponsorship, concluding a 32-year run that turned the golden arches into an integral part of the fan experience across generations. The decision behind the McDonald’s FIFA partnership split marks a pivotal moment in modern sports advertising.

The move follows the chain’s largest-ever World Cup activation. Although the 2026 campaign reached over 110 countries and generated business growth, its performance fell short of internal benchmarks.

However, this transition does not signify a total exit from sports marketing. Instead, it highlights a major strategic shift in how McDonald’s builds cultural relevance and measures advertising return on investment.

According to reports from Adweek, the 2026 World Cup campaign was created by Wieden+Kennedy New York, representing McDonald’s single largest marketing push of the year. Publicis’ Starcom is McDonald’s media agency.

The overall strategy featured limited-edition menu items, interactive digital experiences, collectible merchandise, and high-profile ambassador partnerships with soccer legends such as David Beckham, Ronaldinho, Thierry Henry, and rising star Lamine Yamal.

In official statements, the company noted that the goal of the McDonald’s FIFA campaign was to extend the excitement beyond stadium seats—connecting matches directly to restaurant visits, mobile app engagements, and watch-party gatherings among fans.

Despite the scale of this effort, Ian Borden, Chief Financial Officer at McDonald’s, acknowledged during the Q2 2026 earnings call that while the McDonald’s FIFA campaign drove customer engagement, the overall results missed internal expectations.

This disclosure arrived during a period of slower domestic growth in the United States, though executives did not attribute the slowdown entirely to the soccer push.

💡 Key Takeaway: The activation was by no means a commercial failure, but the financial metrics failed to justify the aggressive targets established prior to the tournament.

The end of the agreement between McDonald’s and FIFA reflects a wider re-evaluation of the fast-food giant’s commercial strategy.

Based on insights from Adweek and MarketingDirecto, McDonald’s is aiming to rely less on borrowed IP—such as major global sports tournaments, entertainment franchises, and third-party cultural partnerships.

Instead, the company plans to double down on building and expanding its owned brand assets, proprietary characters, and direct customer experiences.

Morgan Flatley, Global Chief Marketing Officer at McDonald’s, emphasized that the corporation is streamlining its marketing calendar to execute fewer, higher-impact initiatives.

This pivot does not mean abandoning sports entirely. The brand will maintain selected regional partnerships, including its Formula 1 sponsorship in Latin America and its title sponsorship of France’s Ligue 1.

However, the role of these alliances is changing: rather than serving as the central pillar of global marketing, sports sponsorships will complement an internal brand identity built directly by McDonald’s.

Is Sports Sponsorship Measurement Evolving?

The McDonald’s FIFA breakup takes place in an era where sports broadcasting continues to command huge advertising investments.

An analysis by EMARKETER, referencing data from Dentsu, indicated that 77% of global Chief Marketing Officers planned to increase their spend on sports sponsorships throughout 2026.

Yet, massive global reach no longer guarantees strong commercial returns.

Today, brand marketers must connect ad exposure with concrete business metrics: incremental sales, customer acquisition, purchase frequency, profitability, and long-term brand equity.

While a sponsorship can deliver billions of impressions and trend across social platforms, it does not automatically prove to be a better investment than owned channels, retail media networks, programmatic ads, or direct-to-consumer experiences.

💡 Industry Question: How much should brands pay to partner with global events when they could invest those same dollars into assets and experiences they fully control?

For Mexico—one of the three host nations for the 2026 World Cup—the end of the McDonald’s FIFA deal holds special relevance.

The tournament unlocked major commercial opportunities for food, beverage, e-commerce, telecom, and entertainment brands seeking to capitalize on fan enthusiasm through localized promotions.

McDonald’s participated heavily across host markets with dedicated menu items and fan activations leveraging its long-standing soccer heritage.

However, its decision to walk away from global McDonald’s FIFA ties underscores that even the most recognized sports assets must justify themselves against strict business objectives.

For advertisers across Mexico and Latin America, this move reinforces the need for marketing strategies that extend beyond event visibility. Integrating first-party data, loyalty programs, digital experiences, and clear attribution models helps keep marketing campaigns profitable long after the final whistle.

Although McDonald’s did not publicly disclose the cost of its FIFA agreement or granular ROI figures, its decision brings to light a growing tension between traditional sponsorship value and owned digital ecosystem growth.

After 32 years, McDonald’s is not stepping away from sports as an ad channel. Instead, it is reassessing how much value it gets from a borrowed audience versus the direct relationships it can build and retain on its own.

title: "The women's game in Britain in 2027 is looking like it could be a good year": Emma Raducanu staying away best for her long-term hopes
article_text:
Emma Raducanu has been backed to bounce back, but staying away from the sport as of right now is perhaps her best bet in the long run.

Greg Rusedski said that he sees her bouncing back in 2027 despite her suffering another setback recently in her injury recovery as he spoke on Off Court with Greg, his podcast.

But adding Raducanu to the mix, he said, will help to further a burgeoning women's tennis scene in Britain, which has seen Harriet Dart win in Guangzhou, Sonay Kartal recently reach the Wuhan final, and Katie Boulter have also shown green shoots of life.

Raducanu has not been on court since Queen's, she pulled out of Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament due to a lower leg stress fracture. It means she has fallen from World No.31 in the WTA Rankings after her Queen's run and she is now down to World No.106. This is not high enough to guarantee entry to all WTA 1000 tournaments.

Raducanu has recently returned to the practice courts at the National Tennis Centre in London and posted a clip of herself serving on social media. The former US Open champion is now British No.5 and was recently surpassed by Harriet Dart following her win in the final of Guangzhou.

However, Rusedski believes Raducanu will bounce back in the next year. "No question about it, this is probably good for her to have this period away and keep on building her game so she can stay healthy and consistent.

"I know she’s putting in the hours and the hard work, and hopefully she can find that love and joy that she had in Queens before the unfortunate injury.

"It seems like she has a consistent team now, and the women's game in Britain in 2027 is looking like it could be a good year.

"There are a few little questions on the men's side with their health. Arthur Fery has been the one to kind of save this year for British men's tennis, without his result at Wimbledon and his breakthrough this year, it wouldn’t be such a good picture.

"Norrie has been an amazing career top ten player. Jack Draper, we know his potential, so I hope in 2027 we are not talking about injuries, especially with Brits. Please… all healthy and all playing week in, week out."

title: LIV Golf star admits DP World Tour has 'ruffled some feathers' with fresh 2027 decision
article_text:
Victor Perez has admitted the DP World Tour's position on LIV Golf's proposed 2027 plans has 'ruffled some feathers', with the Frenchman among those still weighing up what comes next.

The three-time DP World Tour winner, who joined Martin Kaymer's Cleeks GC at the start of the 2026 season, is yet to commit to LIV Golf's next chapter as uncertainty continues to surround the breakaway league.

Speaking to Today's Golfer ahead of the Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship at Yas Links, Perez suggested the DP World Tour's stance on players signing up to LIV Golf for 2027 had brought matters to a head.

The DP World Tour's position on membership has effectively forced players to confront a decision that many might otherwise have preferred to put off.

Rather than keeping their options open, those considering LIV Golf now face the prospect of having to choose between the breakaway league and their DP World Tour status.

Perez admitted the situation had 'ruffled some feathers' and prompted players to think about their futures earlier than expected.

"The potential ban for the LIV players in 2027, I think has definitely ruffled some feathers and made a lot of the guys make early decisions," Perez told Today's Golfer.

The Frenchman also acknowledged just how important the DP World Tour is to him personally, having spent much of his professional career competing on the circuit.

"I've played the Challenge Tour, I've played DP World since 2019, played a couple years in America in the middle. This has been the tour that I've grown up playing and watching," he explained.

Perez is now taking legal advice before making a decision and insists he is in no rush to commit to either side, with contracts, negotiations and the precise terms still needing to be considered.

"I still want to be informed with everything and know that everything has been reviewed by lawyers and the whole lot and make the best educated decision," he told Ben Parsons of Today's Golfer. .

"I'm not a person to be emotional and quick to the answer. I just want to make sure everything has been triple checked and looked after and then make the best educated decision once all the info."

The uncertainty has been compounded by the departures of Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton, with Perez admitting that losing two players of their calibre would be a 'massive blow' to LIV Golf's competitive strength.

"With Jon [Rahm] leaving and Tyrrell [Hatton] leaving, they're obviously two huge names that were like top five players for the last few years on LIV, so obviously from a competitive standpoint, it's a massive blow for LIV," said Perez.

While LIV Golf still boasts several high-profile players, none bigger than two-time major champion Bryson DeChambeau, Perez acknowledged that the overall standard of competition remains an important factor when considering his future.

He pointed to Dustin Johnson, DeChambeau, Cameron Smith and Joaquin Niemann as players who could continue to provide a strong competitive environment.

"They're still world-class players," he said.

Perez was also refreshingly honest about his own standing in the game, admitting he is not yet among the very best players in the world.

"I'm unfortunately not one of the elite top, top players. I would say I'm a strong player, but I'm not in the elite level yet," he said.

"So you want to make sure you have enough of those guys to play against week in and week out to level your game and see where you are."

Perez has enjoyed considerable financial success since joining LIV Golf, earning close to $3.5 million across 11 starts and recording two runner-up finishes in Europe.

However, the financial rewards are only one part of the equation. The opportunity to continue playing on the DP World Tour is another major consideration, particularly with the potential prize of a debut Ryder Cup appearance at Adare Manor in September 2027.

Of course, Perez would first need to produce the performances to put himself in contention for a place in Luke Donald's European team, but remaining eligible for the DP World Tour could help keep that ambition alive.

The 2023 Abu Dhabi Championship winner is currently 53rd in the Race to Dubai standings and is fully focused on finishing his season strongly in Abu Dhabi and Dubai this month.

Perez confirmed that he wants to concentrate on the two DP World Tour playoff events before making a final decision, although he admits the wider situation remains difficult to predict.

"There's just the lawsuit going on and obviously people committing and a lot of people still being quite undecided," he explained.

"It's hard to know what the future of either tour will look like and similar for DP World."

He also suggested that some players could still be hoping for a route back to the PGA Tour, although he acknowledged that a deal for returning LIV golfers currently appears unlikely.

"If there's one thing we learned is that deals can be made really late and then people can get quite late exemptions," Perez said.

"It's an overall fluid situation where people are coming and going and making phone calls."

Whether that ultimately leads to a return to the DP World Tour or another season with LIV Golf remains unclear.

With the league's 2027 plans still taking shape, Perez is in no rush to make a decision.

While he may not be one of LIV Golf's biggest names, his eventual choice will offer another insight into how players are assessing the league's future.

title: How Ireland’s gambling reforms are changing sports sponsorship
article_text:
Ireland’s gambling reforms place several questions at the centre of sports sponsorship: who receives the funding, who sees the advertising and which gambling activity is being promoted. The Gambling Regulation Act 2024 treats sponsorship, branded merchandise and digital advertising as distinct issues. Its implementation is phased, making the commencement of individual provisions as important as their wording.

The February 2026 commencement order, reproduced in the Law Reform Commission’s July 2026 consolidation, brought parts of the licensing and enforcement framework into operation. However, it expressly excluded Section 159 on sponsorship and several advertising provisions. The Act’s passage therefore cannot be treated as the date every marketing restriction became enforceable.

For a sports organisation considering a partnership, that distinction separates existing obligations from changes requiring further commencement. A contract extending over several seasons needs to account for that sequence. Announcements about licensing do not, by themselves, establish when a particular sponsorship or advertising restriction applies.

Section 159 sets out prohibitions on sponsorship by business-to-consumer and business-to-business gambling licensees. Its scope includes clubs or teams with child members, events aimed at children and events where most spectators or competitors are children. It also covers premises used by the relevant organisations and public activities appealing to children. Attendance and membership are separate tests within the same sponsorship provision.

The Act defines sponsorship broadly, including public or private contributions whose aim, or direct or indirect effect, is to promote gambling. Calling a payment a donation would not, on its own, settle how that definition applies.

The membership test matters beyond the age of a senior squad. A club containing adult and junior sections cannot assess the statutory wording solely by looking at who plays in its first team. The identity of the sponsored organisation, its membership and the premises involved are separate questions to examine.

A sports partnership promoting an online casino raises questions about both the sponsorship arrangement and the distribution of advertising. A stadium sign, a club’s social post and a paid video campaign are different forms of exposure. Bundling them into one commercial package does not remove the need to assess each element.

For advertising arrangements on social media or video-sharing services, Section 146 provides for an account and subscription requirementonce commenced: the intended recipient must have an account on the service and have subscribed to the licensee’s account. Following a sports club’s page is not the same as subscribing to a licensee. The wording concerns arrangements made by a licensee with another person, so the nature of the advertising relationship also matters.

Section 151 addresses branded clothing and merchandise intended for children, alongside distribution at events children may attend. It also contains a twelve-month exception for certain supplies following its commencement. Youth replica clothing and event giveaways therefore raise questions distinct from the wording of a senior-team sponsorship agreement.

These distinctions give clubs a practical basis for reviewing what a partnership actually includes. Agreements can identify the organisation receiving support, the products being promoted and the advertising channelscovered. They can also specify how material will be withdrawn or replaced if a relevant provision becomes operative during the contract.

The reform does not justify treating every commercial relationship as an identical transaction. Its provisions draw boundaries around recipients, audiences and promotional activity. A useful assessment follows those boundaries, checking commencement and the applicable wording before reaching conclusions about a particular sports partnership.

Leinster name Leo Cullen replacement for 2027/28 season

Noel McNamara said “I am delighted that I am returning to Leinster Rugby as Head Coach in 2027. This is one of the most prestigious roles in world rugby and it is an honour to be given this responsibility.I am very grateful to UBB and in particular Laurent Marti and Yannick Bru for supporting me in availing of this opportunity. title: Rugby sevens: South Africa silver, France gold at Dakar 2026 · SNA
article_text:
South Africa trailed 21-5 at half-time in Monday's final at Stade Iba-Mar-Diop and lost 26-19. Jake Dave scored and converted two second-half tries to drag them back into it, but Gaspard Laharrague's score for France stopped the climb. South Africa go home with silver; Argentina took bronze, beating Canada 36-5.

They had rarely been troubled before that: 43-5 against Senegal, 24-17 against Canada and 34-7 against Germany in the pool, then 24-12 over Argentina in the semi-final, with two tries from Rosco Williams. Team South Africa singled out their second half in that game.

The official sheet shows where the final went. France scored three tries before the break and gave up one, to Darnell Delport. Simon Laharrague finished with 16 points from two tries and three conversions out of three. Dave's 14 accounted for every South African point after the interval. France had arrived in form, having beaten Canada 58-0 in their semi-final.

The hosts ended on a win. Beaten 19-5 by Japan in the fifth-to-eighth bracket, they edged Uganda 10-5 in the seventh-place game, according to the official sheet and Senegalese site Wiwsport. Uganda, who lost 22-0 to Germany, finished eighth. Three of the eight teams in the men's tournament were African.

The women's tournament finishes on Tuesday, with Kenya and Madagascar already sure of a semi-final. The gold medal match is at 17:03 GMT. Fixtures are on our Dakar 2026 page.

title: Ireland team to face Argentina: Sam Prendergast dropped
article_text:
Ireland begin their Nations Championship autumn campaign this Friday night with a tough test against Argentina at the Aviva Stadium.

Andy Farrell's side face a challenging run of fixtures, including a meeting with the Springboks, and will be keen to make a strong start ahead of finals weekend.

Farrell's squad largely picks itself, particularly with the injuries to Jack Conan and Caelan Doris.

The main question is whether the head coach opts for any rotation, although that seems unlikely given Argentina's quality.

Hugo Keenan, Mack Hansen and Rob Baloucoune have established themselves in the back three, while Stuart McCloskey looks certain to start at inside centre after some impressive recent performances.

Robbie Henshaw gets the nod at outside centre, with Garry Ringrose and Bundee Aki also considered. However, McCloskey and Henshaw appear to be Ireland's strongest partnership.

Jamison Gibson-Park is another guaranteed starter, provided he is fit.

Fly-half is the most difficult position to call, with Ciaran Frawley and Sam Prendergast competing for the role following Jack Crowley's injury.

Prendergast has struggled to impress in recent outings, making Frawley the more appealing option.

Both players have plenty to prove as they battle to become Crowley's deputy ahead of the World Cup.

The front row of Andrew Porter, Dan Sheehan and Tadhg Furlong looks settled, with Furlong now available after avoiding a ban. Joe McCarthy and James Ryan are the established second-row pairing.

title: Ryder Cup: Lee Westwood has 'no regrets' about turning down chance to captain Team Europe to play on LIV Golf
article_text:
Lee Westwood was one of the candidates to captain Team Europe at the 2023 Ryder Cup before he joined LIV Golf; Westwood is yet to sign with LIV 2.0 and says the breakaway league are yet to present him with "anything agreeable"

Lee Westwood has "no regrets" about turning down the chance to captain Team Europe at the 2023 Ryder Cup to join LIV Golf, as the former world No 1 revealed he is yet to sign with LIV 2.0.

During a wide-ranging interview on The Chipping Forecast podcast, the 53-year-old said he was currently "unemployed" and added LIV 2.0 had not presented him with "anything agreeable" for the league's proposed relaunch in 2027.

Westwood has represented Team Europe at the Ryder Cup on 11 occasions, having tied Sir Nick Faldo for the most appearances at the biennial tournament during his last outing at Whistling Straits in 2021.

- What golf is live on Sky Sports and when? Full TV listings

Having worked as a vice-captain under Thomas Bjørn at the 2018 Ryder Cup in France, the Englishman was one of the DP World Tour's leading candidates to be appointed captain for the tournament in Rome in 2023.

"Whistling Straights had happened and then quite shortly after that I had a conversation with [DP World Tour chief executive] Guy Kinnings, where he talked about the Ryder Cup captaincy and the captain in Italy," Westwood, who joined LIV Golf in 2022, said.

"It was put to me whether I'd like to be Ryder Cup captain, and I had started discussions with LIV. I think I asked: 'If I did go to LIV, could I still be Ryder Cup captain?'

"They didn't say no, but it was made clear that there would be very little chance of it, and I made the decision to go to LIV.

"You make calls in life, don't you?" Westwood added. "You make a choice, and I have no regrets over the choice I made."

The DP World Tour dictates a player cannot be a European Ryder Cup captain or vice-captain if they decline membership to the tour or fail to fulfil their minimum event obligations.

Henrik Stenson was later named captain for 2023 before he also joined LIV Golf, with the baton ultimately being handed to Luke Donald.

Westwood, who jointly holds the record for the most appearances for Europe at a Ryder Cup, was asked whether he would consider being captain in the future.

"I don't know, I get asked that question a lot," Westwood said. "I've always just wanted to play, I love playing golf.

"When I was vice captain, everybody has a little say in the team room, and I said to the guys: 'You better enjoy it as much as you can because when it's gone, you really miss it, and I'll tell you one thing worse than playing practice rounds in a Ryder Cup is watching other people playing practice rounds in a Ryder Cup.'

"I loved being a Ryder Cup player and getting in that environment. I don't know whether I'd have been a good Ryder Cup captain, because of what I said in France. I don't know whether I would have liked watching."

Delving further, Westwood said: "I'm not good at really pushing control.

"That's one of the reasons I started playing golf, I played a lot of football and rugby and cricket before taking up golf. The reason I enjoy playing golf is because the buck stops with me.

"I didn't want to have to rely on other people and that probably goes back to a little bit of the reason why the Ryder Cup captaincy wasn't really that higher priority.

"When push came to shove, it wasn't the be-all and end-all for me. I'm not sure I wanted it enough."

LIV Golfers have a deadline of November 16 to reapply for their DP World Tour memberships, and Westwood says he is deliberating whether to do so.

Should he reapply, he would face a 10-tournament suspension for his decision to resign his DP World Tour membership.

"I haven't signed up to anything anywhere, I haven't made a decision on anything yet," Westwood said.

"I am yet to have everything put in front of me and I have not really had any dialogue with the DP World Tour.

"I know if I sign up, I've then got to serve a 10-tournament suspension. I've looked at the schedule, and I feel like the first event I could play in on the DP World Tour will be the Turkish Airlines Open, which is the first week in May, so I haven't looked any further.

"There's nothing that's been presented to me that was agreeable for LIV 2.0. There are still a lot of things that would need fine-tuning; deadlines have come and gone, and I've heard nothing on whether I have to sign or not.

"I haven't signed [for] 2.0. So, I literally am unemployed."

All Blacks issue statement after member of security dies at Edinburgh hotel
article_text:
The All Blacks and New Zealand Rugby are mourning the loss of their long-time head of security, Logan Cadwallader, after a medical incident at their Edinburgh hotel.

Cadwallader had been part of the All Blacks family for over ten years and travelled with the side frequently throughout his tenure as the head of security.

All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie said the side will honour Cadwallader and the “legacy he has left on the All Blacks”.

“Logan has been a big part of the All Blacks family for a long time. He was the ultimate team man, loved and trusted by all and a true professional,” Rennie said.

“He looked after all of us, players and staff, and he was a good mate to many in this team. We are all devastated. Our thoughts are with his wife, Nannette, his children, Trey, Brooke and Mia, and his wider family and friends. As a team, we will honour Logan and the legacy he has left on the All Blacks.”

New Zealand Rugby Chief Executive Steve Lancaster extended the organisation’s deepest sympathies to Cadwallader’s family during this time.

“Logan was a valued and trusted member of the management group over the past decade, and he will be greatly missed by everyone who worked alongside him. On behalf of New Zealand Rugby, I extend our deepest sympathies to his family and friends at this very difficult time.”

NZR also recognised Cadwallader’s wide-ranging contribution to New Zealand.

“New Zealand Rugby also acknowledges Logan’s service to the country, at the highest level of the New Zealand Defence Force. Logan served in the New Zealand Army and New Zealand Special Air Service Regiment (NZSAS), with deployments to some of the world’s most demanding environments including Bosnia, East Timor, Afghanistan and the Solomon Islands. His service to his country, and the values he carried from it, were reflected in everything he did for the team.”

title: 'Women's rugby is moving at an incredible pace': PWR set for 2026/27 season
article_text:
The new league season will start on Friday 20 November when Loughborough Lightning host Trailfinders Women beneath the Friday night lights at DPD Stadium at Franklin’s Gardens.

That same weekend, Sale Sharks will host three-time champions Gloucester Hartpury, incumbent champions Saracens will host Leicester Tigers and Bristol Bears will travel to Harlequins.

It has already been confirmed that the league finale will take place at the Twickenham Stoop. Last year, Saracens claimed the title with a 52-14 win over Trailfinders Women in front of 8,009 supporters.

In the World Rugby Women’s 15s Dream Team of the Year 2026, 10 of the 15 players selected have plied their trade in the competition over the past 12 months before going on to star in Test rugby.

Genevieve Shore, JAECOO PWR Executive Chair, said: “Women’s rugby is moving at an incredible pace, and the JAECOO PWR is right at the heart of that growth. We genuinely believe we have the best women’s rugby competition in the world, and we’re determined to keep raising the bar.

“We’re not slowing down. If anything, we’re accelerating. This season is about taking everything we’ve built and making it bigger, better and more ambitious. We have the best players in the world competing in our league, all of the Red Roses, the most exciting emerging talent in the game, and clubs that are continuing to invest in making this competition truly world-class.

“There’s a real sense that the JAECOO PWR is now the undisputed destination for the very best players in women’s rugby. That’s something we should be incredibly proud of, but also something we have to keep working hard to deliver.”

Before the new domestic season, PWR has launched its new campaign. ‘The Home of Heroes’ was established following the Red Roses’ Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 campaign and has returned as the league looks to underline its credentials as the world’s best domestic competition.

This year, the league will “level up” following the arrival of numerous international stars.

Ruby Tui, Gabrielle Vernier and Tabua Tuinakauvadra, to name just three, will now call the PWR home, while there has also been movement across the clubs ahead of the latest season.

The campaign takes inspiration from arcade gaming to “celebrate the extraordinary talent, personalities and performances that make the JAECOO PWR special”.

This season will be especially important for women’s rugby, with the first-ever British & Irish Lions Women tour taking place at its conclusion. The best players from England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales are set to tour New Zealand in September 2027.

Shore said: “The first-ever British & Irish Lions women’s series in 2027 is going to be an extraordinary moment for our sport. It’s another huge milestone for women’s rugby and something that everyone involved in the game should be excited about.

“The JAECOO PWR will have a really important role to play in that journey. Our clubs are providing the environment in which the very best players can develop, compete and perform at the highest level. We want to be producing Lions, international stars and the next generation of heroes.

“What’s exciting is that we’re not talking about what women’s rugby might become any more. We’re seeing it happen in front of us. The crowds, the quality, the investment, the players and the ambition are all moving in the right direction.

“Our job is to keep pushing. We want to be recognised around the world as the best league in the world, and we want to make sure that every season gives supporters another reason to fall in love with the competition, our clubs and our athletes.”

title: Six Red Roses stars named in 2026 World Rugby Team of the Year
article_text:
Hot on the heels of Kaipo Olsen-Baker’s crowning as World Rugby Women’s 15s Player of the Year, World Rugby has confirmed its Dream Team of 2026.

On Saturday, Black Ferns back-row Olsen-Baker was handed her award following New Zealand’s 36-7 victory over France in Christchurch. Her teammate, Elinor-Plum King, was also named World Rugby Women’s 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year.

Olsen-Baker, 24, is named in the 2026 Dream Team alongside Black Ferns teammates Braxton Sorensen-McGee, Sylvia Brunt, Ayesha Leti-I’iga and Maiakawanakaulani Roos.

New Zealand’s five players in the Dream Team are surpassed only by England’s six. World Rugby Women’s 15s Player of the Year nominees Megan Jones and Zoe Harrison are included, as are Jess Breach, Maddie Feaunati, Amy Cokayne and Hannah Botterman.

Canada’s Sophie de Goede, Da Leaka Menin and Olivia Apps are also included, while Léa Champon is France’s sole representative.

15. Braxton Sorensen-McGee (New Zealand)

The World Rugby Women’s 15s Dream Team of the Year 2026 was selected by an expert panel comprising Fiona Coghlan (Ireland), Lena Corson (France), Abby Gustaitis (USA), Heather Moyse (Canada), Shannon Parry (Australia), Melodie Robinson (New Zealand) and Danielle Waterman (England).

Following a global fan vote, Pauline Bourdon Sansus’ try against England in the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations has been named Women’s 15s Try of the Year.

The scrum-half’s effort was voted ahead of tries from Olivia Apps (England v Canada, 19 September), Abi Burton (England v Australia, 12 September) and Léa Champon (France v Scotland, 9 May).

Brett Robinson, World Rugby Chair, said: “Congratulations to Pauline on winning Try of the Year and to all 15 players selected in the Dream Team.

“These awards recognise the exceptional skill, creativity and outstanding performances we have seen throughout 2026, and are a fitting way to celebrate the players who have delivered so many memorable moments on the international stage.

“From established stars to exciting emerging talents, this year’s award winners reflect the incredible depth and ambition of the women’s game.

“As we bring the 2026 international window to a close, there is much to celebrate, and I congratulate all those recognised for their outstanding contributions to another fantastic year of women’s rugby.”

title: Alexander Zverev faces potential fresh complaint as Paris Masters director confirms plans
article_text:
Alexander Zverev’s complaints about the tennis balls used on the ATP Tour may crop up again at the Paris Masters.

The new world No 1 lost in three sets to Alex De Minaur in the semi-final of the Vienna Open on Saturday as his record against the top 10 fell to 3-9.

When the 29-year-old was a break down in the first set, Zverev took umbrage with the Dunlop tennis balls the ATP 500 event was using.

In one instance, he asked the chair umpire, “Do you think it’s normal to play with these balls in a tennis tournament?”

This followed on from the German being among a contingent of players to openly criticise the Wilson balls and the conditions in Montreal this year.
